cases.title: The first witness
cases.brief: Aisha's account takes us from Hira to a household conversation. Which sequence does the report support?

evidence.title: A place of seclusion
evidence.text: The account identifies Hira as the setting of the first encounter.

evidence.title: A trusted response
evidence.text: Khadija reassures him after hearing what happened.

evidence.title: A further conversation
evidence.text: Khadija takes the account to Waraqa ibn Nawfal.

answers: Hira, then Khadija's reassurance, then Waraqa.
Waraqa is present inside the cave.
The report gives an exact Gregorian day.
cases.conclusion: The report supports that sequence. It does not place Waraqa in Hira or provide an exact Gregorian date.
cases.hint: Follow the movement from the cave to the conversations afterward.

passages.arabic:
ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ
خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ
ٱقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ ٱلْأَكْرَمُ
ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَ بِٱلْقَلَمِ
عَلَّمَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ
passages.translation:
Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth,
Createth man from a clot.
Read: And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous,
Who teacheth by the pen,
Teacheth man that which he knew not.

cases.title: The gathering at Safa
cases.brief: A gathering tests what the clans already know about the speaker. What can be established from Ibn Abbas's report?

evidence.title: A public summons
evidence.text: The Prophet ﷺ calls clans of Quraysh to Safa.

evidence.title: A question about trust
evidence.text: He asks whether they would believe a warning about approaching cavalry.

evidence.title: The response
evidence.text: Their reply acknowledges his truthfulness before the warning.

answers: The warning draws on an acknowledged record of truthfulness.
Every person present immediately accepts the message.
The report identifies the exact year of the gathering.
cases.conclusion: The report supports the acknowledgment of truthfulness. It does not say everyone accepted, and it supplies no exact CE year.
cases.hint: Separate what the audience says about trust from how every individual responds.

cases.title: After the rejection
cases.brief: Aisha asks about a particularly difficult experience. Which response is actually described?

evidence.title: The painful encounter
evidence.text: The report recalls rejection after approaching Ibn Abd Yalail.

evidence.title: An offered action
evidence.text: The Angel of the Mountains offers to bring the mountains down.

evidence.title: The response
evidence.text: The Prophet ﷺ declines and expresses hope for future descendants.

answers: He declines destruction and hopes for future worshippers.
The offered destruction is carried out immediately.
The report gives an exact date for an annual observance.
cases.conclusion: The stated response is hope for descendants, not the destruction offered. No exact anniversary is established by this report.
cases.hint: Distinguish the offer from the answer to it.

cases.title: Two in the cave
cases.brief: Abu Bakr describes a moment of danger during the migration. Which conclusion stays within this brief report?

evidence.title: The narrator
evidence.text: Abu Bakr recounts being in the cave with the Prophet ﷺ.

evidence.title: The concern
evidence.text: He fears that looking down would let the pursuers see them.

evidence.title: The reassurance
evidence.text: The reported reply reassures Abu Bakr about Allah's presence with them.

answers: The report records concern followed by reassurance.
This report describes a spider spinning a web.
This report names every person involved in the route.
cases.conclusion: The brief report establishes the concern and reassurance. It does not mention a spider's web or provide a full route list.
cases.hint: Avoid importing familiar details that are not present in the cited report.

passages.arabic: إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِذْ أَخْرَجَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ثَانِىَ ٱثْنَيْنِ إِذْ هُمَا فِى ٱلْغَارِ إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَـٰحِبِهِۦ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَا ۖ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَيْهِ وَأَيَّدَهُۥ بِجُنُودٍ لَّمْ تَرَوْهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ٱلسُّفْلَىٰ ۗ وَكَلِمَةُ ٱللَّهِ هِىَ ٱلْعُلْيَا ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
passages.translation: If ye help him not, still Allah helped him when those who disbelieve drove him forth, the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us. Then Allah caused His peace of reassurance to descend upon him and supported him with hosts ye cannot see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the nethermost, while Allah's Word it was that became the uppermost. Allah is Mighty, Wise.

cases.title: The pursuer's request
cases.brief: Suraqa pursues the travelers, but the encounter changes. What does he request before they continue?

evidence.title: A pursuit
evidence.text: Suraqa describes setting out after the travelers.

evidence.title: A changed situation
evidence.text: He recounts his horse stumbling and later sinking at the forelegs.

evidence.title: A written assurance
evidence.text: He asks for a statement of safety, which Amr ibn Fuhayra writes.

answers: A written assurance of safety.
A declaration that every future pursuer has already converted.
A complete map of the remaining journey.
cases.conclusion: The report specifies a written assurance of safety. The other conclusions add claims not made in these clues.
cases.hint: Look for the request made after Suraqa approaches them.

cases.title: Where is the market?
cases.brief: A report about brotherhood includes a generous offer and an independent response. What does Abd al-Rahman ask for?

evidence.title: A bond
evidence.text: The account pairs Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf with Sad ibn al-Rabi.

evidence.title: An offer
evidence.text: Sad offers substantial help from his property.

evidence.title: The reply
evidence.text: Abd al-Rahman offers a blessing and asks to be shown the market.

answers: To be shown the market.
To be appointed ruler of the city.
To forbid anyone else from trading.
cases.conclusion: The report identifies the market request and subsequent trading. It does not support the claims about political appointment or excluding other traders.
cases.hint: Focus on the reply to Sad's offer.

cases.title: A direction changes
cases.brief: News reaches people who are already praying. Which detail should a careful reader preserve?

evidence.title: An earlier direction
evidence.text: Al-Bara describes prayer toward Jerusalem.

evidence.title: A narrated uncertainty
evidence.text: The duration is given as sixteen or seventeen months.

evidence.title: New information
evidence.text: A person who prayed with the Prophet ﷺ conveys the new direction to others.

answers: The report preserves uncertainty between sixteen and seventeen months.
The report gives exactly sixteen months with no uncertainty.
The report says every prayer before the change was invalid.
cases.conclusion: The narrator's sixteen-or-seventeen wording should remain visible. The other answers either erase uncertainty or introduce an unsupported conclusion.
cases.hint: A small uncertainty is evidence too; do not edit it out.

passages.arabic: قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ ۖ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضَىٰهَا ۚ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ ۚ وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنتُمْ فَوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُۥ ۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ لَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمْ ۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَـٰفِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ
passages.translation: We have seen the turning of thy face to heaven (for guidance, O Muhammad). And now verily We shall make thee turn (in prayer) toward a qiblah which is dear to thee. So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship, and ye (O Muslims), wheresoever ye may be, turn your faces (when ye pray) toward it. Lo! Those who have received the Scripture know that (this revelation) is the Truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.

cases.title: The archers' instruction
cases.brief: The archers receive an instruction covering more than one possible outcome. What made leaving the position a problem?

evidence.title: A commander
evidence.text: Abdullah ibn Jubayr commands the archers in this report.

evidence.title: The instruction
evidence.text: They are told to remain until a message reaches them, even if either side appears to be winning.

evidence.title: A decision
evidence.text: Some leave after seeing an apparent victory and the prospect of spoils.

answers: The instruction explicitly covered an apparent victory as well as danger.
No instructions had been given about the position.
Every archer leaves and the report gives no exceptions.
cases.conclusion: The report makes the instruction explicit. An apparent victory did not cancel it. The absolute claim about every archer goes beyond these cards.
cases.hint: Read the condition about apparent victory, not just the condition about danger.

passages.arabic: وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُۥٓ إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُم بِإِذْنِهِۦ ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلْتُمْ وَتَنَـٰزَعْتُمْ فِى ٱلْأَمْرِ وَعَصَيْتُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ مَآ أَرَىٰكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَ ۚ مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ ۚ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ ۖ وَلَقَدْ عَفَا عَنكُمْ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
passages.translation: Allah verily made good His promise unto you when ye routed them by His leave, until (the moment) when your courage failed you, and ye disagreed about the order and ye disobeyed, after He had shown you that for which ye long. Some of you desired the world, and some of you desired the Hereafter. Therefore He made you flee from them, that He might try you. Yet now He hath forgiven you. Allah is a Lord of Kindness to believers.

cases.title: The journey's purpose
cases.brief: Negotiators ask why the travelers have come. What purpose is stated in the Hudaybiyah account?

evidence.title: The journey
evidence.text: The account describes the approach to Hudaybiyah.

evidence.title: A stated purpose
evidence.text: The Prophet ﷺ explains that they have come for Umrah rather than to initiate fighting.

evidence.title: Negotiation
evidence.text: The narrative proceeds through messages and agreement terms.

answers: The stated purpose is Umrah, and negotiation follows.
The travelers state that they have come only for trade.
The report says no negotiation takes place.
cases.conclusion: The report explicitly distinguishes the intended Umrah from initiating battle. The existence of negotiation is part of the account.
cases.hint: Separate a stated purpose from later tensions during the journey.

passages.arabic: ۞ لَّقَدْ رَضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ يُبَايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ فَعَلِمَ مَا فِى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَأَنزَلَ ٱلسَّكِينَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَثَـٰبَهُمْ فَتْحًا قَرِيبًا
passages.translation: Allah was well pleased with the believers when they swore allegiance unto thee beneath the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, and He sent down peace of reassurance on them, and hath rewarded them with a near victory;

cases.title: Who receives the banner?
cases.brief: An announcement makes people wonder who will receive a banner. Which identification is supported?

evidence.title: An announcement
evidence.text: The banner is to be given the next morning to a person described favorably.

evidence.title: Anticipation
evidence.text: Those present hope to receive it.

evidence.title: The outcome
evidence.text: The report names Ali ibn Abi Talib as its recipient.

answers: Ali ibn Abi Talib receives the banner in this report.
The recipient is chosen by a public vote described here.
The report never identifies who receives it.
cases.conclusion: The report identifies Ali. Anticipation among the companions is not evidence of a public vote.
cases.hint: Look for the recorded outcome rather than the expectations beforehand.

cases.title: Questions during a truce
cases.brief: Abu Sufyan describes an interview with Heraclius. What setting does the account explicitly preserve?

evidence.title: A narrator
evidence.text: Abu Sufyan reports the exchange to Ibn Abbas.

evidence.title: A period of truce
evidence.text: The account locates it during the truce between the Prophet ﷺ and Quraysh.

evidence.title: Questions and a letter
evidence.text: Heraclius asks questions, and the account includes the Prophet's ﷺ letter.

answers: The interview occurs during the truce described by the narrator.
The report states that Heraclius publicly converts immediately.
The conversation happens before any prophetic mission begins.
cases.conclusion: The truce is explicit. The account should not be turned into an assertion of public conversion that it does not establish.
cases.hint: An interested response and a public conversion are different claims.

cases.title: News from a distant land
cases.brief: A death is announced, and a prayer follows. Which action is recorded in this report?

evidence.title: The news
evidence.text: Abu Hurayra recounts the announcement of al-Najashi's death.

evidence.title: The place
evidence.text: The group goes to the prayer ground and forms rows.

evidence.title: The prayer
evidence.text: The report records four takbirs in the funeral prayer.

answers: A funeral prayer in rows with four takbirs.
A journey by the entire group to attend a burial abroad.
An exact CE date is supplied in the report.
cases.conclusion: The report records the prayer and its four takbirs. It does not describe the group traveling abroad or give an exact Gregorian date.
cases.hint: Concentrate on what the group does after receiving the news.
